properties.statement: cap:content-store is built and its surface check passes, yet the shipped binary does the one thing that check says it must not do: it INVENTS a blob directory nobody chose. ver:content-surface passes and claims 'A SERVER WITH NO --content-path CONFIGURED REFUSES BY NAME instead of inventing a directory'. But crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs:30 declares #[arg(long, default_value = "./reflow2-content")], so main.rs:809 and :881 always pass Some(default) and the refusal at service.rs:2464 is UNREACHABLE from the real binary. The test proving the refusal, a_server_with_no_content_store_says_so_instead_of_choosing_one (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs:2795), builds ReflowService::in_memory(), whose builder default is content_path: None (service.rs:2425) — a state the shipped server can never be in. So the check is green against a configuration that does not ship. The store has also never held anything: content_manifest returns entries [], total_bytes 0, store_root './reflow2-content' for a directory that exists nowhere on disk, and of 136 Fragment nodes ZERO carry a content_ref, so missing:[] is honest rather than reassuring. Both ver:content-store and ver:content-manifest remain PLANNED. Consequence, unexercised only because content_put has never been called: the first put would create ./reflow2-content relative to the server's CWD, while .gitattributes already carries 'reflow2-content/** binary' assuming repo root and .gitignore never mentions it — so committed-by-design blobs would land at a cwd-dependent, unignored path. service.rs:2458's own doc comment already states the correct rule, citing req:no-silent-fallback: 'Fails loud rather than defaulting to a directory nobody chose.' Two adjacent files contradict each other and the default is the culprit.
